memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished; he punishes the children and their children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation.'" - Exod 34:7b (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the other half of God's self-description, and we must not skip it because it is uncomfortable.

God forgives — and God does not simply wave sin away. If a judge released every guilty person without dealing with the crime, we would call him corrupt, not kind. God's mercy is never at the expense of His justice.

The line about children and grandchildren troubles many readers, so let us handle it honestly. Scripture is clear elsewhere that God does not condemn children for their parents' guilt: "The one who sins is the one who will die" (Ezek 18:20). What this verse describes is the real, observable way sin's consequences ripple through families — patterns of anger, addiction, unbelief and bitterness passed down through generations. Any of us who have watched a family for fifty years know this is simply true.

But look at the proportions. Consequences to the third and fourth generation; love maintained "to thousands." Mercy vastly outweighs judgement in God's own accounting.

And here is the resolution the whole Bible drives toward: the guilty were not left unpunished, and we were not destroyed. The punishment that brought us peace fell on Christ (Isa 53:5). God remained perfectly just, and we received perfect mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take God's justice as seriously as His mercy?
2. What sinful patterns in your family line do you want to see broken in Christ?
3. How does the cross satisfy both God's justice and His love?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, You are just and You are merciful. Thank You that at the cross Jesus bore what justice required. Break in me every pattern that dishonours You. Amen.
